name: Abdelhak Achik
milestone_by_age_26: Won gold medal in bantamweight at the 1983 Mediterranean Games in Casablanca at age 24, and was Moroccan national senior champion from 1978.
early_history_summary: Started boxing at age 8 at the Khachabate Al Hay Mohammadi boxing school in Casablanca, introduced by neighborhood champion Mohamed Hajji and trained by Mohamed Zarougui. Had his first competitive fight in 1977 at age 18, joined the junior national team, and won the Moroccan national senior championship in 1978 at age 19.
family_context_summary: Grew up in the Hay Mohammadi neighborhood of Casablanca; his brother Mohamed Achik was also a boxer. Parental occupations and financial status not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. A neighborhood champion, Mohamed Hajji, introduced him to boxing rather than a family member.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early boxing school, dedicated trainer, national team pipeline, sibling in sport, working-class urgency
evidence_summary: Achik started boxing at age 8 in a Casablanca neighborhood boxing school, introduced by local champion Mohamed Hajji and trained by Mohamed Zarougui, who immediately identified his potential. He won the Moroccan national championship at 19 and the Mediterranean Games gold at 24. His brother Mohamed was also a boxer, suggesting a family-domain connection, though parental background is not documented. The national team pipeline and sustained coaching from Zarougui were key accelerators.
starting_point: Born in 1959 in a working-class neighborhood of Casablanca, Morocco; family background not documented beyond his brother also being a boxer.
current_position: Former Olympic bronze medalist boxer who became a national boxing trainer and co-founded a boxing school with his brother Mohamed Achik; residing in Morocco as of 2025.

trajectory.event: Joined the Khachabate Al Hay Mohammadi boxing school in Casablanca, introduced to boxing by neighborhood champion Mohamed Hajji.
Had his first competitive fight and was integrated into the Moroccan junior national team.
Won the Moroccan national senior championship in flyweight (51 kg).
Won gold medal in bantamweight at the Mediterranean Games in Casablanca.
Won Olympic bronze medal in featherweight at the Seoul Olympics.
Won gold at the Arab Championships and began transitioning to coaching.
Won bronze at the Mediterranean Games in Greece and launched a boxing school with brother Mohamed.

name: May-Britt Moser
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; she was still a psychology student at the University of Oslo with one student publication. Her Nobel Prize-winning grid cell discovery came in 2005 at age 42, and her PhD was completed in 1995 at age 32.
early_history_summary: Studied psychology at the University of Oslo starting in the early 1980s, where she met Edvard Moser. They published a student paper together and began working with neurophysiologist Per Andersen for their master's thesis, building a water maze lab from scratch.
family_context_summary: Born on a small sheep farm in Fosnavåg, Norway; youngest of five children; father was a carpenter and mother cared for the household.
evidence_summary: Moser grew up on a small sheep farm in rural Norway and was the first in her family to pursue higher education. She studied psychology at the University of Oslo where she met her future husband and collaborator Edvard Moser. By age 26 she was still a student with one student publication; her Nobel Prize-winning work on grid cells came decades later in 2005.

name: Aafia Siddiqui
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; she won a $5,000 student research award at MIT in 1992 at age 20, but this is a minor student grant. Her PhD was completed in 2001 at age 29, and her notoriety stems from post-2001 terrorist-related activities.
early_history_summary: Born in Karachi to an affluent family; father was a British-trained neurosurgeon and mother an Islamic teacher. Moved to the US in 1990, attended University of Houston, then transferred to MIT to study biology on a full scholarship. Won a $5,000 Carroll L. Wilson Award as a sophomore in 1992.
family_context_summary: Born into an affluent Urdu-speaking Muhajir family in Karachi; father was a British-trained neurosurgeon, mother was an Islamic teacher and social worker connected to General Zia-ul-Haq's regime. Sister is a Harvard-trained neurologist.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a neurosurgeon and mother was politically connected; sister Fowzia is a Harvard-trained neurologist, suggesting a family culture of academic and professional achievement.
evidence_summary: Siddiqui came from an affluent, educated Pakistani family with strong political connections. She attended MIT on a full scholarship and won a $5,000 student research award at age 20, but this is a minor student grant rather than a material career milestone. Her PhD was completed at age 29, and her notoriety stems from post-2001 terrorist-related activities.

name: Abbey Lee Kershaw
milestone_by_age_26: Walked 29 shows at New York Fashion Week 2008 and debuted at the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in 2008 at age 21, after being named 'Next Superstar' by Models.com in December 2007.
early_history_summary: Won the Australian Girlfriend Model Search in 2004 at age 17, signed with Chic Management, and moved from Melbourne to Sydney after high school. Was scouted at a beach by Kathy Ward of Chic Management, then signed with Next Management in 2007 and relocated to New York City.
family_context_summary: Born in Melbourne to Kerry, a psychologist, and Kim Kershaw, a former VFL footballer turned financial adviser. Middle child with an older sister and younger brother. Had significant childhood health issues including meningitis and a knee tumor.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Kim Kershaw played professional Australian rules football (VFL) for Richmond and Hawthorn, providing a sports-performance family background, though not directly in fashion.
primary_early_advantage_tags: model search win, top agency signing, physical edge, fashion capital relocation, scout discovery
evidence_summary: Kershaw won the Girlfriend Model Search at 17 and was scouted at a Sydney beach by the same agent who discovered Miranda Kerr. Her father was a former professional footballer turned financial adviser, providing a middle-class platform. Her natural 180cm height and distinctive look gave her a physical edge. By 2008 at age 21, she walked 29 shows at NY Fashion Week and debuted at Victoria's Secret, after being named Models.com's 'Next Superstar.'
starting_point: Born in 1987 in Melbourne, Australia to a psychologist mother and a former VFL footballer father turned financial adviser; middle-class upbringing with significant childhood health issues.
current_position: Working as an actress based in Los Angeles; net worth estimated at ~$4 million; appeared in Horizon: An American Saga (2024) and other films since transitioning from modeling.

trajectory.event: Won the Australian Girlfriend Model Search and signed with Chic Management.
Signed with Next Management, moved to New York City, and was named 'Next Superstar' by Models.com.
Walked 29 shows at New York Fashion Week and debuted at the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show.
V magazine dubbed her a supermodel; Models.com listed her as an 'Industry Icon'.
Made feature film debut in Mad Max: Fury Road and began transitioning from modeling to acting.
Appeared in Horizon: An American Saga Chapter 1 alongside Kevin Costner.

name: Bill Burr
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; he first performed stand-up at age 23 in March 1992 and moved to New York City in 1994, but his first TV appearance came in 1996 at age 28 and his first special in 2003 at age 35.
early_history_summary: Born in Canton, Massachusetts to a nurse and a dentist. Graduated from Emerson College in 1993 with a communications degree. First performed stand-up on March 2, 1992 at age 23 while still in college, winning a Boston college comedy competition.
family_context_summary: Born to Linda Ann, a nurse, and Robert Burr, a dentist, in Canton, Massachusetts. Raised Catholic of German and Irish descent.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; parents were a nurse and dentist with no apparent entertainment industry connection.
evidence_summary: Burr grew up in a middle-class suburb of Boston and graduated from Emerson College. He started stand-up at 23 in 1992, but by age 26 (June 1994) he had only just moved to New York City and was performing at open mics. His breakthrough came years later with TV appearances starting in 1996 and his first special in 2003.

name: Kazuyo Sejima
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; she was working as an employee at Toyo Ito's architecture office. She opened her own studio in 1987 at age 31 and won the Pritzker Prize in 2010 at age 54.
early_history_summary: Graduated from Japan Women's University in 1979 with a degree in architecture, completed her master's in 1981, then worked at Toyo Ito and Associates from 1981 to 1987 before opening her own studio.
family_context_summary: Born in Hitachi, Ibaraki Prefecture, Japan. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Sejima studied architecture at Japan Women's University and completed her master's in 1981. By age 26 (1982), she was working as a junior employee at Toyo Ito's architecture office. She did not open her own studio until 1987 at age 31, and her Pritzker Prize came in 2010 at age 54. No material independently verifiable milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Jüri Tarmak
milestone_by_age_26: Won silver medal at the 1971 European Indoor Championships in high jump at age 25, and was a member of the Soviet national team from 1970 at age 24.
early_history_summary: Took up athletics in 1963 at age 17, following his father Aadu Tarmak who was the Soviet discus champion in 1943-44. Won Estonian SSR championships in 1965-67, then joined the Soviet national team in 1970 at age 24.
family_context_summary: Born in Tallinn, Estonia to Aadu Tarmak, who was the Soviet champion in discus throw in 1943-44 and won Estonian SSR shot put and discus titles in 1945-46.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Aadu Tarmak was a Soviet discus champion and Estonian SSR title-holder in shot put and discus, providing direct athletic domain heritage.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father Soviet champion, athletics from age 17, Soviet national team, Dynamo Leningrad, physical stature
evidence_summary: Tarmak was born into a sporting family in Tallinn; his father Aadu was the Soviet discus champion in 1943-44. He took up athletics at 17 following his father's path, won Estonian SSR titles at 19-21, and joined the Soviet national team at 24. He won European Indoor silver at 25 and Olympic gold at 26, becoming the last straddle-technique Olympic champion.
starting_point: Born in 1946 in Tallinn, Estonia (then Estonian SSR, Soviet Union) to Aadu Tarmak, a Soviet discus throw champion, providing a direct athletic family lineage.
current_position: Died on June 22, 2022 at age 75 in Tallinn, Estonia; final roles included founder of investment company Broker Baltic AS and vice-president of the Tallinn Stock Exchange.

trajectory.event: Took up athletics, following his father Aadu Tarmak's path as a Soviet discus champion.
Won the Estonian SSR high jump championship, beginning a three-year reign as regional champion.
Became a member of the Soviet national team and won bronze at the Soviet Championships.
Won silver medal at the European Indoor Championships in Sofia.
Won Olympic gold medal in high jump at the Munich Olympics, the last champion to use the straddle technique.
Retired from competitive athletics and began studying economics at Leningrad State University.
Returned to Estonia and founded investment company Broker Baltic AS, later becoming vice-president of the Tallinn Stock Exchange.
Died on June 22, 2022 in Tallinn, Estonia.

name: Clarence Seedorf
milestone_by_age_26: Won the UEFA Champions League with Ajax in 1995 at age 19, having already become Ajax's youngest-ever debutant at 16 and won the Eredivisie title in 1993-94.
early_history_summary: Started playing football at age 6 in local amateur sides, was recruited to Ajax's youth academy at age 10 through Johan Cruyff's talent agency. Made his professional debut for Ajax on November 29, 1992 at age 16 years and 242 days, becoming the youngest-ever Ajax debutant.
family_context_summary: Born in Paramaribo, Suriname; moved to Almere, Netherlands at age 2. Father Johann Seedorf was a former football player and talent agent; both parents worked in health service. Grew up in a footballing family with two younger brothers who also became professional footballers.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Johann Seedorf was a former player and football talent agent who guided Clarence and his brothers into the sport. The Seedorf family is a Dutch-Surinamese footballing dynasty producing multiple professional players.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Ajax academy, football family, Cruyff talent agency, Van Gaal coaching, golden generation peers, early debut
evidence_summary: Seedorf was born in Suriname and moved to the Netherlands at age 2 into a footballing family; his father Johann was a former player and talent agent. He was recruited to Ajax's elite youth academy at age 10 through Johan Cruyff's talent agency. He debuted professionally at 16 (Ajax's youngest ever), won the Eredivisie at 17-18, and the Champions League at 19. The Ajax golden generation under Van Gaal and his family's football connections were key accelerators.
starting_point: Born in 1976 in Paramaribo, Suriname to Johann Seedorf, a former football player and talent agent, and a nurse mother; family immigrated to the Netherlands when he was 2, living modestly in Almere.
current_position: Working as senior sports advisor and consultant for Esteghlal Tehran FC; net worth estimated at ~$20 million; resides primarily in Europe.

trajectory.event: Made professional debut for Ajax on November 29, becoming the club's youngest-ever debutant at 16 years and 242 days.
Won the Eredivisie title with Ajax as a key first-team midfielder under Louis van Gaal.
Won the UEFA Champions League with Ajax, defeating AC Milan in the final.
Won his second UEFA Champions League with Real Madrid.
Won his third UEFA Champions League with AC Milan, becoming the only player to win it with three different clubs.
Won his fourth UEFA Champions League with AC Milan.
Retired from playing and became manager of AC Milan, though dismissed after a few months.
Appointed as senior sports advisor and consultant for Esteghlal Tehran FC.

name: Joachim Trier
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; he had just graduated from the National Film and Television School in 2000 and made his first short film Pietà. His feature debut Reprise came in 2006 at age 32.
early_history_summary: Born in Copenhagen to a Danish father and Norwegian mother, raised in Oslo in a filmmaking family. Attended European Film College in Denmark (1995-97), then the National Film and Television School in England, graduating in 2000. Made short films Pietà (2000), Still (2001), and Procter (2002).
family_context_summary: Born into a filmmaking family; father Jacob Trier was the sound technician of The Pinchcliffe Grand Prix (1975), and grandfather Erik Løchen was artistic director of Norsk Film and a filmmaker.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a sound technician in Norwegian film and grandfather was a filmmaker and artistic director of Norsk Film, providing deep film industry lineage.
evidence_summary: Trier grew up in a prominent Norwegian filmmaking family with both his father and grandfather in the industry. He attended film school in Denmark and England, graduating in 2000 at age 26. His first short film Pietà was made that year, but his feature debut Reprise didn't come until 2006 at age 32. No material independently verifiable milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Quino
milestone_by_age_26: By 1954 at age 22, his cartoons were being regularly published in major Argentine magazines including Rico Tipo, Tía Vicenta, and Dr. Merengue, establishing him as a professional cartoonist.
early_history_summary: Started studying at the Escuela de Bellas Artes de Mendoza at age 13 in 1945, guided by his uncle Joaquín Tejón, a professional illustrator. Both parents died by 1948 when he was 16. He left school in 1949 to become a cartoonist, sold his first illustration, and published his first humor page in Esto Es magazine.
family_context_summary: Born to Spanish immigrant parents from Andalusia in Mendoza, Argentina; father was a commercial employee, mother a housewife. Both parents died during his adolescence (mother 1945, father 1948), leaving him orphaned at 16.
parent_family_domain_summary: His uncle Joaquín Tejón was a professional illustrator and graphic designer who awakened his vocation for cartooning and provided early mentorship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: uncle illustrator mentor, orphaned at 16, art school, Buenos Aires magazine scene, early professional publication
evidence_summary: Quino was born to Spanish immigrant parents in Mendoza and orphaned at 16, which deepened his dedication to drawing. His uncle Joaquín Tejón, a professional illustrator, mentored him from childhood. He studied at Bellas Artes from age 13, left school at 17 to pursue cartooning, and by 22 was regularly published in major Argentine magazines. The loss of both parents and isolation catalyzed his artistic focus.
starting_point: Born in 1932 in Mendoza, Argentina to Spanish immigrant parents from Andalusia; father was a commercial employee, mother a housewife, both dying during his adolescence.
current_position: Died on September 30, 2020 at age 88 in Mendoza, Argentina; final status: one of the most celebrated cartoonists in the Spanish-speaking world, creator of Mafalda.

trajectory.event: Enrolled at the Escuela de Bellas Artes de Mendoza after his mother's death, guided by his uncle Joaquín Tejón, a professional illustrator.
Abandoned art school after his father's death to pursue cartooning professionally; sold his first illustration.
Published his first humor page in Esto Es magazine and became a regular cartoonist in Rico Tipo, Tía Vicenta, and Dr. Merengue.
Published his first compilation book Mundo Quino and created the character Mafalda for an advertising campaign.
Mafalda comic strip first published in Primera Plana magazine, launching what would become an iconic series.
Stopped drawing Mafalda at its peak to focus on other cartooning work.
Awarded the Prince of Asturias Award and the French Legion of Honour.
Died on September 30, 2020 from a stroke in Mendoza, Argentina.

name: Jô Soares
milestone_by_age_26: Began his television career in 1958 at age 20 at TV Rio, writing and performing in comedy shows, after making his film debut in 1954 at age 16.
early_history_summary: Born in Rio de Janeiro to a businessman father and housewife mother. Studied in Switzerland as a teenager where he became interested in theater. Returned to Brazil when his father's business failed and began taking acting classes. Made his film debut in 1954 at age 16 and started in television in 1958.
family_context_summary: Born to Orlando Heitor Soares, a businessman from Paraíba, and Mercedes Leal Soares, a housewife. Maternal great-grandfather was a diplomat and governor of Espírito Santo. Studied in Switzerland as a teenager.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family had diplomatic and political connections; great-grandfather was a diplomat and governor. Father was a businessman whose business failure forced Jô's return from Switzerland to Brazil.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Rio TV industry, Swiss education, family social status, early film debut, Brazilian TV boom
evidence_summary: Soares was born into an affluent Brazilian family with diplomatic lineage and studied in Switzerland as a teenager. When his father's business failed, he returned to Brazil and pivoted to entertainment, making his film debut at 16 and starting in TV at 20. Rio de Janeiro's position as the center of Brazilian television in the late 1950s provided a frontier ecosystem for his early career.
starting_point: Born in 1938 in Rio de Janeiro to an affluent businessman father and housewife mother with diplomatic lineage; studied in Switzerland as a teenager before family financial difficulties forced a return to Brazil.
current_position: Died on August 5, 2022 at age 84 in São Paulo; final role: Brazil's most prominent late-night talk show host (Programa do Jô, 2000-2016); left an estate of approximately R$50 million.

trajectory.event: Made his professional film debut in 'O Rei do Movimento' in Brazilian cinema.
Began television career at TV Rio, writing and performing in comedy shows.
Joined Rede Globo, Brazil's largest network, starring in comedy shows like Faça Humor, Não Faça Guerra.
Launched his own prime-time sketch show Viva o Gordo, creating over 200 characters for a weekly audience of ~70 million.
Moved to SBT to host his first nightly talk show, Jô Soares Onze e Meia.
Returned to Rede Globo to host Programa do Jô, which ran for 16 years and 8,000+ episodes.
Retired Programa do Jô after 16 years on air.
Died on August 5, 2022 in São Paulo, leaving an estate of approximately R$50 million.

name: Ștefan Birtalan
milestone_by_age_26: Won the World Championship gold medal with Romania in 1970 at age 22, and was named to the senior national team in 1968 at age 20.
early_history_summary: Trained in handball, volleyball, basketball and athletics as a teenager. Debuted in handball at age 16 with Rapid CFR Jibou in 1964. Moved to Baia Mare in 1966, joined the junior national team, and was elevated to the senior national team in 1968 at age 20.
family_context_summary: Born in Zalău, Sălaj, Romania. Family background not documented in reviewed sources beyond his multi-sport athletic upbringing.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Romanian national team, Steaua București, multi-sport background, exceptional physical stature, early debut at 16
evidence_summary: Birtalan was born in Zalău, Romania and trained in multiple sports as a teenager before focusing on handball. He debuted at 16 with Rapid CFR Jibou, joined the junior national team at 18, and the senior national team at 20. His exceptional physical attributes (194cm, 96kg, cannon arm) combined with the Romanian national team pipeline and Steaua București club system propelled him to a World Championship gold at 22. Family background is not documented.
starting_point: Born in 1948 in Zalău, Sălaj, Romania; family background not documented, but grew up as a multi-sport athlete in the Romanian sports system.
current_position: Died on May 27, 2024 at age 75 in Bucharest; final roles included handball coach at Steaua București and the Qatar national team.

trajectory.event: Debuted in handball with Rapid CFR Jibou in the Cluj Regional Championship.
Included in the Romanian junior national handball team and moved to Baia Mare.
Elevated to the Romanian senior national handball team.
Won World Championship gold with Romania in France and joined Steaua București.
Won his second World Championship gold, was top scorer with 43 goals, and named World Player of the Year.
Won Olympic silver medal at Montreal, averaging nearly six goals per game and named top scorer.
Won the European Champions Cup (EHF Champions League) with Steaua București.
Died on May 27, 2024 in Bucharest after a long illness.
